answer: Divergent response ledger. Each identity answers a random challenge from its own entropy and prior answers; hashes are compared pairwise. Clones cannot diverge, so copies emit identical hashes and collapse to one identity. A tundra deployment still works because challenges queue. Honest agents may wander across devices but keep their chain. A crystal check rejects two ledgers sharing a chain. Attackers pay a separate 256-bit seed plus per-round storage per identity.
